Maria V: Pushed an nsys + perfetto trace from a mixed INT8/FP8 rollout that started seeing a regression on decoder latency. TL;DR: dequant kernels and some host-copy spikes line up with KV cache misses. link: https://perfetto.dev/trace/abcd1234 :eyes:
Jason K: pinging the runtime team — I see a 12% p99 increase on 2x A100 runs compared to last week. is this the new int8-dequant path?
Eli P: can you drop the raw nsys summary? helps me match kernels to queue times.
Maria V: pasted below the relevant slice from nsys (trimmed):
```
GPU Activity:  72%  (compute)
Kernel: dequantize_fp8_to_fp32      18.7ms  42%
Kernel: int8_matmul_dispatch         4.2ms   10%
Memcpy H2D                            1.1ms   2%
Memcpy D2H                            6.4ms  14%  <-- spikes around KV evict windows
Kernel: kv_lookup_batched            3.9ms   9%
```
Maria V: noteworthy: when seq_len > 1024 we see repeated D2H at regular intervals that correlate with `kv_evict` events. Could be host-assisted backup path for cold KV pages.
PerfBot: nsys job 1900456789 finished, profile saved to s3://redwood-profiles/1900456789.qdrep :white_check_mark:
Rachel S: did you compare the mixed-quant codegen vs the pure-int8 path? maybe kernel selection bumped to fp32 fallback for some attention sizes.
Maria V: good call — I ran a microbench toggling kernel selector. With "strict_int8=true" the dequant kernel drops but accuracy drops ~0.7 BLEU on our eval set. With selector on auto it picks FP8 dequant for certain heads which seems slower but keeps accuracy.
Aaron T: can we try two quick experiments: (1) force kv cache warmup earlier so we avoid the H2D/D2H thrash, (2) collect per-kernel occupancy for the dequant kernel?
Jason K: for (1) a cheap heuristic is issue a small prefetch for top-K keys on new sessions. code sample we used before: `enqueue_prefetch(session_id, head_idx, prefetch_n=64)`
Eli P: also capture the kernel launch params. I suspect grid/block dims changed with the FP8 variant and are not saturating SMs. If occupancy low, even a 2ms host-copy can kill p99 due to serialization.
Maria V: attached a short perfetto timeline screenshot (copied events): dequant kernel starts -> 0.9ms later D2H -> next kernel stalls 1.2ms -> kv_lookup runs. Sequence repeats every ~260ms during long contexts.
Rachel S: accuracy tradeoff is real. If we quantize more aggressively we save 20% GPU time but eval drifts. Maybe try mixed precision: int8 matmul + fp16 softmax + fp32 dequant only where needed.
Aaron T: i can instrument a small build that logs `selector_reason` per dispatch (hotpath vs fallback). cheap and non-invasive.
Jason K: agreed. also add sampling for batch sizes in-flight. I want to see whether batching heuristics are collapsing (i.e., tiny batches causing more memcpy overhead).
Eli P: next steps: Maria run (A) warmup-prefetch heuristic + nsys trace, (B) selector-logging build + perfetto timeline, (C) microbench of the dequant kernel with explicit block/grid to test occupancy. I'll take the traces and run kernel-level perf counters.
Maria V: starting (A) now; ETA ~30m. Will post a trimmed trace and summary. Thanks everyone. :thumbsup:
